subject: Information Theory
title: Routing Algorithms
description: A short lesson to help you apply Routing Algorithms.

hook.text: How does a packet in Tokyo reach a server in London in 80 milliseconds? Routing algorithms choose the optimal path.

buildup.text: Dijkstra's algorithm finds the shortest path. Each router maintains a table of best next hops for every destination.

discovery.text: The internet uses two approaches: OSPF for internal networks and BGP for inter-domain routing between providers.

twist.text: Optimal routing is NP-hard for large networks. Real routers use heuristics that are good enough, not perfect.

climax.text: Routing is distributed computation: each router makes local decisions that collectively produce global information flow.

punchline.text: Local decisions, global paths. Routing is distributed intelligence.

quiz.question: Why don't internet routers find globally optimal paths?
options: Optimal routing is computationally too expensive for large networks
